findings.title: [P2] Restrict the duplicate-pick exemption to actually scoped picks
findings.body: The global check treats every publicID-bearing descendant of the event or selected origins as selected, although pick resolution only uses direct children of the designated container. For example, a QML event containing one direct pick and another same-ID pick nested under its origin passes the global duplicate-pick exemption, and the direct pick is accepted as unique. The nested object is outside the documented pick scope, so its shared identity should make the representation unknown. Native selected-origin descendants have the same problem. Apply the duplicate-pick exemption only when every colliding node belongs to the actual scoped `picks` collection.

findings.title: [P2] Check publicID collisions across the document root
findings.body: The global identity index traverses only EventParameters, leaving root-level siblings unchecked. A native document with selected pick `pick:A` inside EventParameters and an outside sibling `<pick publicID="pick_A"/>` passes validation and retains an accepted pick, despite the two IDs mapping to the same candidate. QML root-level identity collisions are likewise ignored. The documented contract explicitly requires whole-document publicID ambiguity checking against selected objects, independently of full schema validation. Traverse the root for collision detection while preserving the existing selection scope.

overall_explanation: Read-only source inspection found two gaps in global identity ambiguity checking that allow conflicting outside-scope objects to coexist with accepted unique picks. Both violate the documented conservative identity contract.
